name: VA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Jennifer McClellan running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
No competitive polling or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to McClellan: a D+17 district, incumbency, and a roughly $1.1 million fundraising advantage over Robert Murray, with markets pricing a near-certain Democratic win. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting competition, the forecast stays at a large Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or major outside spending against McClellan would be the first sign of movement, but nothing currently indicates it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Virginia's 4th District is a solidly Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of about 17 points toward Democrats. Jennifer McClellan, the Democratic incumbent, is running for reelection and has raised over $1.1 million, while Republican Robert Murray has reported little financial activity. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but lacks visible resources.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the incumbent's advantages. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the margin rather than the winner.
